chapter: New Orleans bands, players and halls
title: Downtown bands and district jobs; Dave DePass and Arnold
summary: Foster says only a few bands had regular jobs, the downtown bands working the district at Huntsnagle's, and describes hiring and firing by letter.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: So you were talking about George McClellan, last year, he was in the cotton,
dry wood, dry wood, dry wood.

He was a, cotton sampler. Sampler, see, you take cotton and, he's rated somewhere, huh? See, because he taught sitting in Desville. That's right. See? He was another nice trumpet player too. You see, because, you see people, they write those books, but some of those books are so wrong, you see, they don't know those people, see, just like to say, now, you take over your band, them band, them band, there's a very few bands, I can count the names of the bands, that had regular jobs. And all the bands that had regular jobs was the downtown band, the McNoey band, the Superior band, the Imperial band, the Olympic band, a lot of their bands had night jobs in the district. Man was at Royce's, we was at Bill of Phillips, Freddie and them was at Bill of Phillips, we was at Huntsnagle's, Customizing Liberty, see, see. What was the name of your place? Huntsnagle.

see, Eddie Grochet, Eddie Grochet and Huntsnagle, Eddie Grochet, we were at the ship. Yeah, two partners, see, Eddie Grochet, see, now, Manuel had his band on there, Joe had his band, see, well, because we used to work, we were the Superior band, see, when Superior band go, off on gigs, we work in there, we work, see, we'd always have three or four nights in the district. Superior band and the McNally band worked for Huntsnagle, but he didn't, he didn't win with you, because he, he didn't, him, him and Louie Nelson, I was playing with Louie. Yeah, yeah, him and Louie Nelson, now, now, now, now, now, big old Louie, see, big old Louie played with us first, after, see, we had, we had a planet player called Dave DePass, we would have kept Dave, but we won't get rid of Arnall, drummer, that was his brother, that was his brother, but we couldn't get rid of Arnall, unless he could get rid of Dave, so, they used to put letters under your door, and you get fired, man, put a letter, somebody slipped through your door, you make amazing when you find your letter, you got no job, your band.
